reasons: Lake identity gives case_name Olmstead v. United States, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1928-06-04, and year 1928.
Lake citations list official 277 U.S. 438, vendor-neutral 1928 U.S. LEXIS 694, and parallels 48 S. Ct. 564, 72 L. Ed. 944, and 66 A.L.R. 376.
The opinion states the wire insertions were made without trespass on defendants' property and later says there was no entry of defendants' houses or offices.
The majority expressly concludes that the wire tapping did not amount to a search or seizure within the Fourth Amendment.
Lake treatment scope_note supports the Katz-overruling and Jones-revival parenthetical.
residual_risks: The word 'pure' is a gloss; the opinion also relies on the Fourth Amendment text and tangible-material-things reasoning.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Consider replacing 'pure property/trespass framing' with 'physical-invasion/tangible-things framing'.

reasons: The opinion identifies the question as interception of private telephone conversations by wire tapping.
The facts and holding are centrally about wiretapping/electronic surveillance, and the lake treatment fields verify the historical Katz-overruled status.
residual_risks: Title III is not discussed in the 1928 opinion; support is for the broader electronic-surveillance home, not for statutory Title III analysis.

defect.evidence_quote: Neither the cases we have cited nor any of the many federal decisions brought to our attention hold...
defect.problem: The disclosed evidence supports a historical trespass/physical-invasion role, but not the stronger implication that Olmstead is the doctrinal origin of trespass analysis.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the role to 'Historical / physical-invasion framing' or 'Historical / no-trespass rule'.

reasons: The opinion repeatedly turns on no trespass, no entry, tangible effects, and actual physical invasion.
The opinion also situates its analysis in earlier cited cases, so 'origin' is not proven from the disclosed record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Preserve the Trespass home but avoid 'origin' unless the home page or another disclosed source establishes that taxonomy.
